title: Mumbai Faces 10% Water Cut from May 15 Amid El Niño Fears
excerpt: BMC orders citywide supply reduction as reservoir levels hit 28% and IMD warns of a below-normal monsoon season ahead.
body:
Mumbai's civic authority pulled the trigger on a water rationing measure that will touch every household in India's financial capital. Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide announced a 10% water cut across the city starting May 15, citing shrinking reservoir stocks and an El Niño-driven threat to the upcoming monsoon.

**What the BMC decided — and why:**
With the possible impact of El Niño on the monsoon leading to deficient rainfall, the BMC has announced a 10% water cut from May 15 to ensure supply lasts until August. According to the India Meteorological Department, the country is expected to witness below-average rainfall during the southwest monsoon because of developing El Niño conditions, with rainfall predicted at nearly 92% of the long-period average — placing it in the below-normal category.

**How tight are the city's reserves:**
The overall water stock stood at 28.79% on April 27, while the BMC supplies 3,850 million litres daily to Mumbai against an overall demand of 4,300 MLD, leaving a deficit of 250 MLD. To avoid a severe shortage, the civic body plans to reserve additional water from the Bhatsa and Upper Vaitarna reservoirs after obtaining approval from the Maharashtra government — a move BMC believes could stretch existing supply through mid-August. Separately, corporators have moved a notice demanding urgent measures such as protecting groundwater, fixing leakages, desilting the city's seven lakes, and installing borewells for non-drinking use.

**What to watch next:**
Officials have warned that the situation could worsen significantly if rainfall remains below normal in the upcoming monsoon season — making the Maharashtra government's decision on releasing reserve dam water the critical variable to track in the coming weeks.
